sentences.text: Asteracanthus was one of the largest known hybodonts, reaching lengths of 2 to 3 meters.
Its teeth were high-crowned and multi-cusped, while fin spines featured tubercles rather than the ribbing seen in other hybodonts.
A complete skeleton of this animal was described in 2021 from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen Limestone.
Evidence suggests Asteracanthus may have scavenged on marine reptiles.
The animal was adapted for open marine environments and likely swam just above the seafloor.
Researchers suggest Asteracanthus used its teeth for grasping prey, with side teeth adapted for crushing.
It likely fed on a diverse diet including fish, crustaceans, echinoderms, molluscs, and cephalopods like belemnites.
However, the Paleobiology Database lists the parent group as Acrodontinae and the family as Acrodontidae.
The genus is now considered distinct from Strophodus, with teeth more similar to those of Hybodus and Egertonodus.
Fossils of Asteracanthus have been found in Europe, including Germany, Switzerland, England, and France.
